1.q: At the hawker centre, Uncle puts 4 satay sticks on each of 3 plates. Then he adds 2 more sticks. How many sticks are there now?
1.hint: Add the sticks on the 3 plates first, then the extra ones.
1.why: 3 plates of 4 sticks make 12 sticks. Add the 2 more: 14 sticks.

1.q: Wei Jie looks at the house numbers from 1 to 40 on his lane. He circles each number that ends in 3 or 7. How many numbers does he circle?
1.hint: Look at the ones digit only.
1.why: The numbers are 3, 7, 13, 17, 23, 27, 33 and 37. That is 8 numbers.

1.q: A ribbon is 24 cm long. Mum cuts it into 4 pieces of the same length. How long is each piece?
1.hint: Share the length into equal groups. Which number times 4 makes 24?
1.why: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24, so each piece is 6 cm long.

1.q: The lift in Kumar's HDB block is on floor 6. It goes up 4, then down 5, then up 2. Which floor is the lift on now?
1.hint: Start at floor 6. Count up or down on a number line.
1.why: The floors in order are 6, 10, 5, 7. The lift ends on floor 7.

1.q: Kumar's swimming lesson is in 4 days. Today is Wednesday. On which day is the lesson?
1.hint: Count on one day at a time. Tomorrow is day 1.
1.why: Count on from Wednesday: Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. The lesson is on Sunday.

1.q: A tile has 6 sides. Every side is 3 cm long. An ant walks once all the way round the edge of the tile. How far does the ant walk?
1.hint: Add the side length once for every side.
1.why: Add the sides: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 18 cm.

1.q: Two bags hold 20 buns in all. One bag has 6 more buns than the other. How many buns are in the bigger bag?
1.hint: If the bags held the same, how many would each have? Then move some buns across.
1.why: The bigger bag has 13 buns and the smaller has 7. They add to 20 and differ by 6. The bigger bag has 13 buns.

1.q: The school bus leaves at 9 o'clock in the morning for a trip. The trip lasts 5 hours. At what o'clock does the trip end?
1.hint: Count on the hours on a clock face. After 12 comes 1.
1.why: Count on from 9 o'clock: 10, 11, 12, 1, 2. The trip ends at 2 o'clock.

1.q: Farhan has 3 T-shirts and 2 pairs of shorts. An outfit is one T-shirt and one pair of shorts. How many different outfits can he make?
1.hint: Pick one T-shirt. How many outfits does it make with the shorts?
1.why: Each of the 3 T-shirts goes with 2 pairs of shorts. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 outfits.

1.q: I think of a number. I double it, then I add 3. My answer is 19. What is my number?
1.hint: Work backwards. Undo the adding first, then undo the doubling.
1.why: Backwards: 19 − 3 = 16, and half of 16 is 8. Check: double 8 is 16, and 16 + 3 = 19.

1.q: A pond has 3 lily pads on Monday. Every day the number of lily pads doubles. How many lily pads does the pond have on Thursday?
1.hint: Doubling means two times as many. Write the number for each day.
1.why: Monday 3, then doubling each day: 3, 6, 12, 24. On Thursday there are 24 lily pads.

1.q: Aunty has 17 cupcakes. A box holds 4 cupcakes. How many boxes does she need to pack all the cupcakes?
1.hint: Count in 4s: 4, 8, 12 ... Is 16 enough?
1.why: 4 boxes hold 16 cupcakes. 1 cupcake is left over, and it needs another box. So she needs 5 boxes.

1.q: Siti has 14 stickers and Ben has 8 stickers. Siti gives some stickers to Ben. Then they both have the same number of stickers. How many stickers does Siti give to Ben?
1.hint: Find how many more stickers Siti has than Ben. Each sticker that Siti gives moves across the gap.
1.why: Siti has 6 more than Ben. Each sticker she gives makes the gap 2 smaller, so she gives half of 6, which is 3 stickers. Check: they both have 11.

1.q: Kaya toast costs $2 each. A cup of hot chocolate costs $1. Mum buys 3 toasts and 2 cups of hot chocolate. How much does she pay?
1.hint: Add the toasts first. Then add the cups of hot chocolate.
1.why: 3 toasts cost $6. 2 cups of hot chocolate cost $2. Together that is $8.

1.q: Jun Hao uses lolly sticks to make a row of squares. One square uses 4 sticks. Two squares joined side by side use 7 sticks. How many sticks do 4 squares joined in a row use?
1.hint: A new square shares one side with the last square. How many new sticks does it need?
1.why: Each new square adds 3 sticks: 4, 7, 10, 13. So 4 squares use 13 sticks.

1.q: Mei Ling starts reading at half past 3 and stops at 5 o'clock. For how many minutes does she read?
1.hint: Half past 3 to 4 o'clock is half an hour. How many minutes is that?
1.why: Half past 3 to 4 o'clock is 30 minutes. 4 o'clock to 5 o'clock is 60 minutes. 30 + 60 = 90 minutes.

1.q: 5 friends meet at the void deck. Every friend gives a high five to each of the other friends, once. How many high fives are there?
1.hint: Call the friends A, B, C, D and E. List the pairs, such as AB.
1.why: A makes 4 high fives. B makes 3 more, C makes 2 more and D makes 1 more: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 high fives.

1.q: Hui Min writes this pattern: 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, ... Each jump is 1 bigger than the jump before. What is the 7th number in her pattern?
1.hint: Write down the jumps: 1, then 2, then 3. Keep going and keep adding.
1.why: The jumps are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The numbers are 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, 22. The 7th number is 22.

1.q: There are 9 children in a line for the water cooler. Hui Min is 3rd from the front. What place is she from the back?
1.hint: Draw the line with dots. Mark Hui Min, then count the children behind her.
1.why: There are 9 children. The 3 children at the front, including Hui Min, are not behind her. So 9 − 3 + 1 = 7 place.

1.q: Mei Ling lists 2-digit numbers whose two digits are the same, such as 22 and 66. How many numbers can she list?
1.hint: Think about the tens digit first. It can be any digit from 1 to 9.
1.why: The numbers are 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, 66, 77, 88 and 99. That is 9 numbers.

1.q: Priya has three number cards: 7, 0 and 3. She uses all three cards to make a 3-digit number. What is the smallest number she can make?
1.hint: A 3-digit number cannot start with 0.
1.why: The first digit cannot be 0, so start with the smallest other card, 3. Then use 0, then 7. The number is 307.

1.q: Xin Yi threads beads in this pattern again and again: pink, green, green, pink, green, green, ... What colour is the 10th bead?
1.hint: Each pattern has 3 beads. The 3rd, 6th and 9th beads are green.
1.why: The pattern starts again after every 3 beads. The 9th bead ends a pattern, so the 10th bead starts a new one. It is pink.

1.q: In the school hall, the front row has 1 chair. The next row has 2 chairs, then 3, and so on up to 6 chairs in the last row. How many chairs are there altogether?
1.hint: Pair up the rows: the first with the last, the second with the one before last.
1.why: Pair the rows: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4. Each pair makes 7. 3 pairs make 21 chairs.

1.q: Siti is taller than Ben. Ravi is taller than Siti. Who is the shortest?
1.hint: Draw three lines. Put the tallest on the right.
1.why: Ravi is taller than Siti, and Siti is taller than Ben. From tallest: Ravi, Siti, Ben. So Ben is the shortest.

1.q: A bun costs $3 and a drink costs $2. Ben pays $10. How much change does he get?
1.hint: Find the cost of the bun and the drink together first.
1.why: The bun and the drink cost $5 together. $10 take away $5 leaves $5.

1.q: A path goes round a pond and is 20 steps long. Aunty puts a pot of flowers every 4 steps, all the way round. How many pots does she need?
1.hint: Draw a circle. Mark a pot every 4 steps. Do not count the starting pot twice.
1.why: 20 steps ÷ 4 steps = 5 pots. Because the path is a loop, the last pot is next to the first one.

1.q: Hui Min pays exactly 30 cents using 10-cent coins and 5-cent coins. She may use only one kind of coin if she likes. How many different sets of coins can she use?
1.hint: Start with no 10-cent coins. How many 5-cent coins make 30 cents? Then try one 10-cent coin.
1.why: With no 10-cent coin: six 5-cent coins. With one 10-cent coin: four 5-cent coins. With two: two 5-cent coins. With three: none. That is 4 sets sets.

1.q: A string has 17 beads. 6 are red and 4 are blue. The rest are yellow. How many beads are yellow?
1.hint: Add the red and blue beads first. Then see how many more make 17.
1.why: Red and blue beads: 10. 17 take away 10 leaves 7 beads.

1.q: In a picture graph, each star stands for 2 children. The swimming row has 7 stars and the badminton row has 4 stars. How many more children chose swimming?
1.hint: First find how many more stars the swimming row has. Then think about what each star is worth.
1.why: Swimming has 3 more stars. Each star is worth 2 children, so 3 stars are 3 × 2, which is 6 children.

1.q: Aisha's art camp starts on the 9th and ends on the 15th. The first day and the last day both count as camp days. How many days is the camp?
1.hint: Write down every date from the first day to the last day. Then count them.
1.why: Count every date from the 9th to the 15th, both included: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15. That is 7 days.
